profile.campus: Manassas, Prince William County, Virginia (Equinix DC14, part of the Washington DC-area IBX network)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's DC14 facility at 7400 Infantry Ridge Road in Manassas, Virginia, part of Equinix's broader Washington DC-area IBX network centered on the nearby Ashburn "Data Center Alley" campus in Loudoun County, the region Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet. Equinix's own published specifications for DC14 describe a two-story, reinforced-concrete building of 42,539 square feet, with N+1 power redundancy, 120v/208v distribution, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; the facility carries a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, and SOC 2 Type II. Equinix has stated DC14 sources wind renewable energy certificates from Texas and Oklahoma and uses LED lighting and hot/cold aisle containment for efficiency. Manassas sits within the wider Northern Virginia data center corridor that also includes Equinix's much larger Ashburn campus, where the company's first two buildings, DC1 and DC2, were established in the late 1990s and DC2 has been described as reputedly the most connected building on earth. DC14 offers colocation in private cages with high-density cooling, smart-hands support, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and Equinix's own Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's website did not provide a founding or opening date for DC14 in the material fetched this session.

Manassas sits roughly 20 miles southwest of the Ashburn core, part of Prince William County's own growing data center corridor distinct from but adjacent to Loudoun County's much larger concentration; Prince William County has separately drawn large hyperscale campus proposals (including from Amazon and QTS/Blackstone) in the years since DC14 was built, reflecting Northern Virginia's data center growth pushing outward from Ashburn into neighboring counties as available Loudoun land and power capacity tighten.

reading.body:
Equinix DC14 is a 42,539 square foot facility in Manassas, Virginia, part of the operator's 15-facility Washington DC metro region, which Equinix positions as North America's largest peering point. The facility publishes no megawatt capacity figure, so its compute potential cannot be assessed against the state or regional benchmark. N+1 power and cooling redundancy indicate this is a production-grade colocation site capable of hosting latency-sensitive workloads, though the specification does not indicate tier level or whether it is designed for high-density AI loads.

Virginia's 326 mapped facilities total 1,375 megawatts in published capacity across 23 sites that report figures. DC14's lack of a published capacity number places it outside the state's measurable deployed base and prevents ranking it among the largest regional assets. Equinix's Ashburn cluster (DC1-DC6, DC10-DC13, DC15-DC16, DC21-DC22) dominates the region as mapped facilities, with the Manassas and Culpeper additions extending the corridor outward.

Without published power capacity, DC14 cannot be read as a constraint or enabler on AI scaling in the DC region. The facility's relevance to grid-constrained AI deployment depends on figures Equinix has not disclosed in its public specification page.
